headline: The reopen priced the war, then sold it: Brent gapped to $105.48 at the 5pm CT open and faded to ~$103.4 in Asian trade on ceasefire-and-diesel supply hopes — while the dollar held near 18-month highs at ~102.2 as December hike odds firmed to ~85% going into CPI week.

chapters.title: US Dollar
chapters.teaser: DXY held ~102.2 near 18-month highs in thin Monday trade — less on the war now, more on the Fed: December hike odds firmed to ~85% going into Wednesday's CPI.
chapters.meaning: What changed: December hike odds firmed from ~80% to ~85% (Reuters, Oct 12), October steady at ~18% — the dollar's prop is rotating from the war bid to the rate bid. The tape itself barely moved: Tokyo shut for Sports Day, US bonds shut for Columbus Day, so today's flatness is thin liquidity, not conviction. Thread: the hawkish hold is in week five — Dec was ~80% priced, claims 197k, and Sunday added zero Fed-relevant data. What it means: confirms the prior thesis — the Fed path into CPI week is unchanged; the only real test is Wednesday's CPI (consensus ~3.6% y/y; the key number is core m/m at 0.2%), then Warsh's IMF-Bangkok dialogue Thursday 10:30pm CT, the last Fed voice before the Oct 17 blackout.
chapters.fx: What to watch: CPI Wednesday 7:30am CT — core 0.3%+ revives the October hike and extends DXY; 0.2% or below cements December-only and squeezes crowded USD longs. Warsh Thursday 10:30pm CT. Thin Monday liquidity (Columbus Day) amplifies headline moves — treat today's tape with caution.
numbers: US 10Y 5.22% Fri (FRED DGS10; bonds closed Mon)
CPI Wed 7:30am CT (cons 3.6% y/y; core m/m 0.2%); Warsh Thu 10:30pm CT

scenarios.base: Hawkish hold rides through CPI week; thin Monday tape consolidates near the highs.
scenarios.bull: Hot CPI (core 0.3%+) revives the October hike — DXY breaks out.
scenarios.bear: Soft core (0.2% or below) plus diplomacy progress — crowded USD longs squeeze and DXY gives back.

chapters.title: Euro
chapters.teaser: EUR/USD probed under the weekend low at 1.1188 in thin Tokyo trade, then steadied at ~1.1201–1.1217 — five straight weekly falls, with Tuesday's French budget plenary as the next live threat.
chapters.meaning: What changed: a thin-liquidity dip under the weekend low (1.1188) that found buyers — EUR/USD recovered to ~1.1217. The euro stays on the defensive for a fifth straight week amid European deficit concerns (Reuters). Thread: the 17-month low at 1.1161 (Oct 5) held last week; Sunday's Ukraine energy-ceasefire theater died within hours (Zelensky called it 'news for me,' Russia struck Zaporizhzhia anyway); OAT–Bund sits ~140–146bp. What it means: confirms the weak-euro thesis — but today's dip was holiday noise, not a break. The real test is Tuesday's French budget plenary, not Monday's tape.
chapters.fx: What to watch: French budget plenary Tuesday 3:00am CT (08:00Z) — the fuse on the OAT–Bund spread; German ZEW Tuesday 4:00am CT (09:00Z); Lagarde speaks Wednesday twice; 1.1161 is the line that matters.
numbers: French plenary Tue 3:00am CT; German ZEW Tue 4:00am CT

scenarios.base: Range holds into Tuesday's plenary; 1.12 area consolidates.
scenarios.bull: A calm plenary plus soft US CPI — 1.1161 holds and the euro bounces toward 1.13.
scenarios.bear: Fiscal stress flares or hot CPI — 1.1161 breaks and the fifth weekly fall extends.

chapters.title: British Pound
chapters.teaser: Sterling did nothing at ~$1.3245 — but Bailey's Oct 8 speech kept the November hike at ~86% priced, and he speaks four times this week starting Wednesday.
chapters.meaning: What changed: Bailey's Oct 8 Istanbul speech landed — hawkish-leaning but non-committal: 'an unwavering commitment to returning inflation to target' while staying 'sceptical of unconditional promises about future interest rates.' November 5 hike odds held at ~86%, so the market read it as confirming the hawkish hold, not a signal shift — and he speaks four times this week (Wednesday through Saturday), so the hike path gets four public tests. Thread: EUR/GBP at ~84.6p is a 16-month sterling high; the 30Y gilt sits above 6%. What it means: confirms the prior thesis — the hawkish-BoE floor stands unchallenged, and on a thin Monday a speech that changed nothing is the whole story.
chapters.fx: What to watch: Bailey's four appearances — Wed 12:30am CT, Thu 2:30am CT, Thu 9:00pm CT (the big one, post-data), Sat 1:45am CT; UK GDP Thursday 1:00am CT (fcst −0.1% m/m) is the growth counterpoint to the hike case.
numbers: UK GDP Thu 1:00am CT fcst −0.1% m/m

scenarios.base: GBP consolidates the 1.32 area; the ~86% November floor holds.
scenarios.bull: A hawkish Bailey into hot UK data — GBP/USD pushes toward 1.34.
scenarios.bear: A negative GDP print plus dovish Bailey — the hike floor wobbles and 1.3180 gets tested.

chapters.title: Japanese Yen
chapters.teaser: USD/JPY eased to ~158.16–158.25 in thin Tokyo trade — the fear gap lower never showed, because the reopen's war pop got sold; now the rate gap owns it again.
chapters.meaning: What changed: the Sunday-open fear bid fizzled — oil faded from $105.48 to ~$103.4 and USD/JPY slipped only ~0.1%, capped under the weekend high of 158.43. Reuters notes the pair has 'stalled on the yen at 158.15 as the threat of Japanese intervention deters speculators.' Thread: BoJ December hike >80% priced (OIS) against the US 10Y at 5.22% — the rate gap pulls toward 159–160 while fear pulls toward 155; CFTC yen longs rebuilt to 62,325 (week to Oct 6). What it means: partially breaks the weekend's fear thesis — Sunday's escalation was sold, not feared. The two-way tug is back to fear vs rate gap, with the gap currently winning.
chapters.fx: What to watch: crude holding above $90 — the downside-support line Tokyo desks are watching; Friday's CFTC update on yen longs; Wednesday's CPI, which reprices the Fed side of the gap.

scenarios.base: Rate gap dominates; USD/JPY consolidates below 159 while intervention talk caps the top.
scenarios.bull: Fresh escalation plus a hot CPI — the fear bid returns and USD/JPY breaks lower through 158.
scenarios.bear: Soft CPI reprices the Fed — the yield gap narrows and 156 comes into view.

chapters.title: Swiss Franc
chapters.teaser: The fear gauge went nowhere — USD/CHF ~0.8306, flat — because the oil fade unwound the haven bid before Monday even started.
chapters.meaning: What changed: nothing moved. The haven gap that was supposed to show at the reopen never arrived — oil's fade from $105.48 to ~$103.4 took the fear out of the pair before Asia opened. Thread: SNB pinned at 0.00% with no domestic rate story; Schlegel speaks Wednesday 11:30pm CT. What it means: confirms the franc's one-dimensional read — it only gets a chapter when fear spikes. Today it gets one line.
chapters.fx: What to watch: any fresh escalation headline — that's the only thing that moves this pair right now; otherwise the franc sleeps until Schlegel.

scenarios.base: CHF drifts with the fear tape — flat while oil fades.
scenarios.bull: Fresh escalation — CHF firms as the pure fear trade.
scenarios.bear: Diplomacy progress — the haven bid leaks out further.

chapters.title: Australian Dollar
chapters.teaser: AUD/USD flat at ~$0.698 — the cleanest risk proxy held its ground through the war weekend, and the RBA minutes land tonight at 7:30pm CT.
chapters.meaning: What changed: nothing for the Aussie overnight — flat in thin Asia. The background headwind: CBA expects the Houthis to keep attacking Saudi energy assets, which supports oil and the USD — a weight on the risk proxies. Thread: RBA on hold at 4.60% after the Sep 29 hike; Australia jobs Wednesday 7:30pm CT (fcst 20.0K, unemployment 4.6%); China CPI Tuesday 8:30pm CT. What it means: the risk-proxy read is parked until tonight's minutes show how hawkish the hiking RBA was — the tone into the Nov 2–3 decision.
chapters.fx: What to watch: RBA minutes tonight 7:30pm CT — any tightening-bias lean supports the AUD's best-in-G10 policy case; Australia jobs Wed 7:30pm CT; China CPI Tue 8:30pm CT.

scenarios.base: AUD trades the risk mood into the minutes — soft on escalation, firm on calm.
scenarios.bull: Hawkish minutes plus a calm reopen — AUD reclaims 0.70.
scenarios.bear: Dovish minutes read as one-and-done — the policy tailwind fades and 0.6930 returns.

chapters.title: Canadian Dollar
chapters.teaser: The oil fade cost the loonie its Sunday offset — USD/CAD ~1.4249 at 18-month CAD lows while Brent slipped to ~$103.4 and the 161bp rate gap keeps owning it.
chapters.meaning: What changed: Brent faded from the $105.48 open to ~$103.4 (−1.4% in Asian trade), thinning the war-premium offset that was supposed to help the loonie; USD/CAD sat near the 18-month low. Thread: Oct 28 BoC hike odds ~25% (from 40% pre-jobs); the US–Canada 2Y gap at ~161bp, widest since February 2025; the number that actually moves Canada's terms of trade is WTI (~$90.50), with the Brent–WTI spread at ~$13. What it means: confirms the tug-of-war thesis — Sunday strengthened the oil hand, Monday's fade weakened it; the rate gap never blinked.
chapters.fx: What to watch: Macklem speaks Wednesday 1:05am CT; Canada CPI Oct 21; BoC Oct 28. The spread is the gauge: toward $15 means Hormuz risk is back in force; toward $5 means the premium is truly unwinding.

scenarios.base: Tug-of-war holds; USD/CAD consolidates 1.42–1.43 into the BoC.
scenarios.bull: Fresh escalation with Brent toward $108 — the oil offset finally bites and the loonie firms.
scenarios.bear: Oil keeps fading and the 161bp gap reasserts — 18-month lows break.

chapters.title: New Zealand Dollar
chapters.teaser: The quietest chapter again — ~$0.561, flat — with the RBNZ's Oct 28 two-way bet (~50% priced) as the only thing on the calendar.
chapters.meaning: What changed: nothing — the kiwi sat out the weekend and the reopen. Thread: RBNZ at 2.75% with Oct 28 a genuine two-way bet (~50% priced, down from ~75%); NZ CPI lands Oct 21, a week before the decision. What it means: thesis stands — this one drifts with risk sentiment into the RBNZ, and Sunday's escalation was just a softer mood.
chapters.fx: What to watch: NZ CPI Oct 21 — the number that settles the two-way bet; RBA minutes tonight (AUD spillover).

scenarios.base: NZD drifts with risk sentiment into the RBNZ decision.
scenarios.bull: RBNZ hikes Oct 28 after all — NZD re-rates higher.
scenarios.bear: RBNZ pauses and sounds done — NZD underperforms the commodity bloc.

chapters.title: Oil
chapters.teaser: Brent opened Sunday at $105.48 (+0.7%) on the weekend war ledger, then faded to ~$103.4 in Asian trade — the market priced the escalation, then sold it on ceasefire-and-diesel supply hopes.
chapters.meaning: What changed: the fade — from $105.48 at the open to ~$103.4 (−1.4% in Asian hours) as markets priced Trump's un-signed Ukraine energy ceasefire and the Russian diesel deal (partial export-ban lift: 300k tons in October) against the weekend's escalation: Riyadh struck twice, a UKMTO-confirmed drone hit on a tanker at Sohar with two Indian seafarers missing, the IRGC's unverified third mine-hit claim, and oil-majors' chiefs pulling out of the Riyadh energy congress (FT). Thread: Goldman raised its December Brent forecast to $90 (from $85) with ~$20/bbl of risk premium in price; Gulf of Mexico crews are redeploying after Hurricane Isaias; Hormuz transits sit at two-month lows. What it means: partially breaks the weekend's premium thesis — the market is fading escalation and buying the supply story. The ~$13 Brent–WTI spread stays the geopolitical-premium gauge: wide means the premium is shipping and geopolitics, not demand.
chapters.fx: What to watch: whether Moscow ever confirms the energy ceasefire; physical diesel cargoes (the deal's real test, not the press release); the MBS call and Trump's decision on joining Saudi strikes; GoM restart figures; the EIA weekly. Spread toward $15 = Hormuz risk back in force; toward $5 = premium truly unwinding.

scenarios.base: Brent drifts $100–106; the market keeps fading escalation until a verified supply shock.
scenarios.bull: An Aramco confirmation of a facility hit or Trump joining the campaign — Brent toward $110+, spread past $15.
scenarios.bear: Ceasefire confirmation or fast GoM restarts — Brent under $100, spread collapses toward $5.

chapters.title: Gold
chapters.teaser: Gold held ~$4,206 (+0.3%) — the war-hedge leg faded with oil, but the anti-dollar leg is loading ahead of Wednesday's CPI.
chapters.meaning: What changed: gold firmed to ~$4,206 in thin trade — up more than 1% on the week (Reuters) — even as the oil fade took the war-hedge heat out of it. Thread: spot was ~$4,195 Friday against the January $5,318 all-time high; the anti-dollar leg waits on Wednesday's CPI — hot core (0.3%+) revives October-hike talk, real yields jump, and that's gold's enemy. What it means: confirms the two-engine read — the haven leg softened with the fade, the dollar leg is all about Wednesday now.
chapters.fx: What to watch: Wednesday's CPI — soft core (0.2%) weakens the dollar leg and re-arms gold toward $4,300; hot core sends it back toward $4,000.

scenarios.base: Gold consolidates $4,100–4,300 into Wednesday's CPI; direction comes from the print.
scenarios.bull: CPI undershoots and hike bets collapse — gold breaks $4,300 and the anti-dollar trade broadens.
scenarios.bear: Hot CPI revives the October hike; real yields jump and gold slides back toward $4,000.
